items.message:
**I will have fresh Aronia berries tomorrow at the market. For most people these berries are too astringent to eat fresh so I've included a list of some of the uses for them.**

**Aronia** (*Aronia melanocarpa*, black chokeberry) — a tough, self-fertile native shrub, hardy to zone 3, that carries the highest anthocyanin load of any temperate fruit. The berries are astringent raw; tannins ease after frost or a stint in the freezer, and almost every use below improves when aronia is blended with a sweeter fruit or given sugar, fat, or fermentation to work against.

🫐 **Juice** — press or steam-juice; cut with apple or grape to make it drinkable straight
🫐 **Jam & jelly** — blend 1:1 or 1:2 with apple, pear, or elderberry; naturally pectin-rich
🫐 **Syrup** — for pancakes, soda water, or a winter tonic by the spoonful
🫐 **Shrub / drinking vinegar** — the acid cuts the astringency better than sugar alone
🫐 **Wine** — a long-standing use; deep color, needs aging to soften tannin
🫐 **Melomel or mead** — pairs well with a light wildflower honey
🫐 **Cordial or liqueur** — vodka or brandy infusion, sweetened after straining
🫐 **Fermented soda** — ginger bug or whey starter, aronia plus honey
🫐 **Kombucha second ferment** — a small handful colors and flavors a whole bottle
🫐 **Dried berries** — raisin-like, good in granola and trail mix
🫐 **Powder** — dried and milled; stirs into smoothies, yogurt, baked goods
🫐 **Fruit leather** — best blended with applesauce as a carrier
🫐 **Pie, crisp, cobbler** — half aronia, half apple or rhubarb
🫐 **Muffins & quick breads** — use frozen, straight into the batter
🫐 **Sauce for meat** — treat like cranberry sauce; excellent with pork, venison, duck
🫐 **BBQ sauce or ketchup** — the tannin gives real backbone
🫐 **Chutney** — with onion, vinegar, warm spices
🫐 **Fruit vinegar** — ferment the juice out past wine
🫐 **Tea** — dried berries steeped alone or with mint and rose hip
🫐 **Infused honey** — dried berries in raw honey, 3–4 weeks
🫐 **Sorbet & ice cream** — fat and sugar tame it completely
🫐 **Gummies or pâte de fruit** — concentrated juice plus pectin or gelatin
🫐 **Natural colorant** — a small amount deep-tints frosting, kraut, kombucha, pickles
🫐 **Dyestuff** — wool and cellulose fiber take a purple-gray with alum mordant
🫐 **Winter wildlife food** — berries persist on the shrub and feed birds into January 

**Vinegars: **I will have Black Currant, Cherry, Siberian Peach, Pear Cider 32 oz -$11 | 16 oz $7.

.

V7 is bringing a familiar favorite back into the spotlight this summer with the launch of its new Cream Soda flavor.

Following the buzz around last summer’s Pink Lemonade edition, the brand is continuing its summer-focused lineup with a flavor inspired by the nostalgic taste of classic cream soda. The new addition comes as part of V7’s refreshed identity, blending a familiar flavor profile with a fresh and modern look aimed at today’s generation.

With its nostalgic twist and new identity, V7 Cream Soda is set to become one of the flavors to watch this summer, giving fans another reason to keep V7 on their radar.
